summary: A cardholder makes ordinary purchases during a billing cycle, stays below the credit limit, receives a statement, and pays the full statement balance before the due date. The scenario is designed to confirm an on-time full-payment path with a statement close and due-date check, preserving the purchase grace period and avoiding late or over-limit fees.
assumptions: The account has no previous balance at the start of this billing cycle, so the purchase grace-period condition is satisfied under clause.6.grace_period.
The cardholder's credit limit is $1000.00, and total posted purchases in this cycle never exceed that limit, so no over-limit fee should arise.
The periodic statement closes on 2025-03-31 and sets a payment due date of 2025-04-25, which is at least 25 days later.
The minimum payment for a $300.00 new balance would be $15.00 under the contract formula (3% of $300.00 is $9.00, so the greater amount is $15.00).
The payment of $300.00 is received and credited on the same day using a standard approved payment method, so it counts as timely under the agreement.
No cash advances, returned payments, disputed charges, illegal transactions, or other default-triggering events occur in this scenario.

Clause.4.credit_limit and clause.6.grace_period are represented with zero-amount notice events because they are behavioral/issuer obligations rather than cash movements, but they are included so the executor can bind them by clauseId as required.
